data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient because it can implement 'active-active' dynamic traffic evacuation that decentralized networks cannot coordinate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure originates within the unified control plane itself (the 'Complexity Paradox').","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The traffic volume exceeds the capacity of the remaining healthy segments during evacuation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A unified control plane allows for the instantaneous rerouting of 100% of traffic away from a failing segment based on real-time telemetry, whereas decentralized services lack the global state necessary to preemptively avoid correlated failures in neighboring nodes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
